candidates.name: Identity-Private Tempo State Isolation
build_steps: Batch all visible pose tracks through one shared pose encoder and one shared bank of tempo-response experts.
Allocate a separate recurrent state, routing history, overlap-add buffer, and decoder accumulator for each active track ID; prohibit cross-track state attention.
Train the counting path with masked-pose reconstruction, temporal augmentation consistency, and response-consistency losses only; use no per-person count or period labels.
Add a cross-person tempo-swap stress test in which one person's speed changes while all other trajectories remain fixed.
Emit one count and confidence value per finalized identity; compute scene total only by summing the emitted vector for diagnostics.
candidates.hypothesis: Strictly isolating temporal state by identity will prevent a fast or abruptly changing person from perturbing another person's local-tempo routing, improving per-person count stability in asynchronous scenes while retaining shared model parameters.

minimum_leakage_free_pilot.data: Freeze a source-disjoint MultiRep train/dev split and checksums; do not access the official test population.
minimum_leakage_free_pilot.protocol: Use supplied tracks first so identity assignment is fixed. Train three independent seeds without per-person count or period labels. Compare identity-private state against stateless windows and a shared scene-state control under clean data and single-person piecewise time warps.
measurements: per-person prediction change on untouched identities after another identity is warped

success: At least 8% relative AvgMAE reduction versus shared scene-state on the piecewise-warp dev set.
At least 3 percentage-point AvgOBO improvement with bootstrap CI excluding zero for the paired difference.
Median absolute count change for untouched identities is at most 0.25 when another identity alone is time-warped.
failure: AvgMAE is more than 3% worse than the stateless-window control on clean supplied tracks.
Untouched identities change by more than 0.5 count on median during the cross-person tempo-swap test.
Routing histories remain indistinguishable across identities despite different imposed tempo profiles.

risk.description: Private state may merely store track length or confidence instead of useful tempo context; the tempo-swap control and state-reset ablations are required to expose this.

unavailable_inputs: A frozen leakage-free MultiRep release and source-disjoint split
Canonical supplied-track files with stable person identifiers
An implemented label-free response-training objective
Official Period-mAP evaluator and paired source-cluster bootstrap
closest_priors: MultiCounter and MultiCounter+ for identity-indexed MRAC outputs and consistency
PAMS for pose-driven self-supervised period adaptation
Generic recurrent tracking systems with per-track memory
Mixture-of-Experts for shared expert weights and learned routing
candidates.why_it_matters: It directly tests whether identity-indexed state is functionally necessary for asynchronous multi-person counting, rather than treating per-person output as a final formatting step.

candidates.name: Supplied-versus-Predicted Track Protocol Pair
build_steps: Define two frozen inference contracts: supplied tracks with dataset identity IDs, and predicted tracks produced without GT boxes or GT object IDs.
Use the identical pose encoder, tempo experts, response reconstruction, and decoder in both contracts; only the track source may differ.
Store frame-level track assignments, confidence, HOTA, IDF1, ID switches, per-person count vectors, and the matching used exclusively for evaluation.
Add a deterministic synthetic-corruption ladder to supplied tracks with independent detection drops, fragmentation, re-entry gaps, and ID switches.
Report count degradation as a function of tracking degradation rather than mixing both protocols into one headline number.
candidates.hypothesis: A paired protocol will isolate counting-model error from identity-association error and reveal which tracking failures dominate per-person count degradation without changing the no-count-label training objective.

minimum_leakage_free_pilot.data: Use one checksum-frozen source-disjoint dev split; generate corruption seeds from stored manifests and keep all corruption parameters independent of count or period annotations.
minimum_leakage_free_pilot.protocol: Run three model seeds under clean supplied tracks, corrupted supplied tracks, and one frozen predicted tracker. Match predictions to GT identities only inside the evaluator.

success: Every published count result is unambiguously tagged as supplied-track or predicted-track.
Synthetic corruption severity produces a monotone increase in median per-person count error in at least 80% of adjacent severity steps.
The protocol attributes at least 80% of predicted-track count failures to one of missed detections, fragmentation, re-entry mismatch, ID switch, or counting-on-correct-track categories.
failure: Any predicted-track run consumes GT boxes or GT object identities.
Protocol matching changes model outputs rather than operating only in evaluation.
More than 20% of count failures remain unclassified because required track artifacts were not saved.

risk.description: The protocol can become bookkeeping-heavy and may expose that tracking, rather than tempo modeling, is the dominant bottleneck.

unavailable_inputs: An authorized leakage-free MultiRep dev release
A frozen external detector, pose estimator, and tracker with disclosed supervision
Official or faithfully reproduced HOTA and IDF1 evaluation
Complete frame-level tracking and prediction artifacts
closest_priors: HOTA and IDF1 multi-object tracking evaluation
Robustness evaluation using synthetic detection and association corruption
candidates.why_it_matters: It prevents oracle-like GT-assisted tracks from being presented as a deployable multi-person system and makes the cost of identity errors visible in the actual per-person count output.

candidates.name: Pose-and-Phase Re-entry State Cache
build_steps: When a track disappears, store a bounded dormant-state record containing its last pose embedding, motion direction, local response phase, uncertainty, and accumulated count mass.
When a new tracklet appears, score re-entry candidates using pose geometry, temporal gap, motion extrapolation, and phase compatibility; do not use GT identity at inference.
Reactivate the best state only when confidence and margin thresholds pass; otherwise begin a new identity state.
Train association scoring from natural or synthetic tracklet splits and temporal augmentations without per-person count or period labels; disclose any external tracker supervision.
Finalize the output vector after a configurable re-entry horizon, retaining aliases so a recovered person receives one count entry rather than one entry per fragment.
candidates.hypothesis: Caching identity-private phase and response state across temporary disappearance will recover count continuity after fragmentation while reducing duplicate person outputs and double counting.

minimum_leakage_free_pilot.data: Create a source-disjoint supplied-track dev diagnostic by masking contiguous pose intervals and replacing post-gap track IDs; generate masks without consulting count or period labels.
minimum_leakage_free_pilot.protocol: Compare no cache, pose-only re-identification, and pose-plus-phase cache over gap lengths of 0.25, 0.5, 1, and 2 estimated cycles; evaluate both isolated gaps and crowded simultaneous re-entry.
measurements: count error added by each gap

success: Recover at least 40% of the fragmentation-induced AvgMAE increase relative to the no-cache system.
Achieve at least 95% precision for automatic fragment merges on the pilot.
Improve person-cardinality F1 by at least 5 percentage points without reducing clean-track AvgOBO by more than 1 point.
failure: False merges exceed 5% or cause more aggregate error than the recovered missed merges.
Re-entry benefit disappears when phase features are removed, indicating the cache is only a generic pose re-identification module.
Dormant-state retention causes unbounded memory growth or requires GT identity at inference.

risk.description: Similar-looking people performing synchronized actions may make phase and pose insufficient for safe re-entry; conservative abstention may limit recall.

unavailable_inputs: Frame-level pose tracks with timestamps and confidence
Crowded re-entry examples or a defensible synthetic gap generator
Stable output matching and person-cardinality evaluation
A frozen policy for maximum dormant-state lifetime
closest_priors: Tracklet re-identification and dormant-track memory in multi-object tracking
Phase-continuity tracking in periodic signal processing
candidates.why_it_matters: Fragmentation otherwise converts one real person into multiple count entries or resets progress, violating the primary requirement that the system return one count per person.

candidates.name: ID-Switch-Resilient State Hypothesis Bank
build_steps: Detect ambiguous associations from tracker confidence, crossing geometry, and sudden pose-state discontinuity.
At an ambiguity, fork only the affected identities' private states into a small set of assignment hypotheses instead of immediately committing to one ID swap.
Advance each hypothesis through the same shared encoder and tempo experts, scoring it with pose continuity, motion plausibility, response-phase continuity, and augmentation-consistency energy.
Prune to a fixed beam and merge equivalent hypotheses; never average state between different candidate identities.
Finalize per-person counts from the highest-confidence identity history and expose ambiguity confidence alongside the count vector.
candidates.hypothesis: Delayed association commitment will preserve per-person count attribution through short crossings and tracker ID switches better than hard propagation, without using per-person count or period labels.

minimum_leakage_free_pilot.data: On a frozen source-disjoint dev set, inject deterministic pairwise ID swaps of 0.5, 1, and 2 seconds at track crossings; injection must not consult counts or periods.
minimum_leakage_free_pilot.protocol: Compare hard tracker IDs, state reset on discontinuity, and a beam of two or four hypotheses across three independent model seeds.
measurements: count-vector permutation error before and after evaluator matching
beam survival of the correct synthetic identity assignment

success: At one injected switch per person-minute, count AvgMAE increases by no more than 25% relative to clean tracks.
The hypothesis bank reduces switch-induced AvgMAE by at least 20% relative to hard ID propagation.
Beam size four stays below 1.8 times the latency and 1.5 times the peak memory of hard propagation on the pilot batch size.
failure: The method improves scene-total count but not identity-matched per-person AvgMAE.
Correct-assignment beam survival is below 70% for one-second swaps.
The method silently merges two people into a single output or relies on GT identity to select a hypothesis.

risk.description: Hypothesis branching can become combinatorial in dense scenes; bounded beams may discard the correct identity history during long or multi-way crossings.

unavailable_inputs: Track association logits or reconstructable ambiguity scores
Crossing-heavy evaluation clips
A deterministic ID-switch injector
Per-frame latency and memory instrumentation
candidates.why_it_matters: An ID switch can leave the scene-total count unchanged while exchanging or corrupting individual counts, so robustness must be assessed at the count-vector level.

candidates.name: Ragged Shared-Compute Multi-Person Runtime
build_steps: Represent all active track windows as one ragged batch with explicit identity indices and masks.
Run the pose encoder and tempo-specialized expert weights once per batched tensor operation while gathering and scattering only compact identity-private states.
Cache overlapping-window pose features and reuse them during normalized overlap-add reconstruction; invalidate cache entries only when their source frames change.
Keep parameter count independent of the number of people while allowing state and response-buffer memory to grow explicitly with active identities.
Return an ordered list of per-person count, confidence, and track identifier records; measure scene total only as a derived diagnostic.
candidates.hypothesis: Ragged batching and overlap reuse will make multi-person inference substantially cheaper than invoking a complete single-person counter independently for every track while preserving identity-private outputs exactly.

minimum_leakage_free_pilot.data: Use checksum-frozen pose tensors or synthetic tiled copies of leakage-free dev tracks; no labels are needed for the scaling measurements.
minimum_leakage_free_pilot.protocol: Benchmark 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 concurrent identities at fixed clip length and window schedule. Compare independent model invocation, ordinary padded batching, and ragged shared execution on the same hardware and commit.
measurements: numerical difference in per-person response and count

success: At 16 active identities, latency is at most 55% of independent per-person invocation while all count outputs differ by no more than 0.01 before rounding.
Peak memory at 16 identities is at least 30% lower than padded batching for a workload with variable track lengths.
Model parameter count is invariant with person count, and all person-dependent state allocations are documented as O(P) rather than described as constant-time.
failure: Shared execution changes any rounded per-person count relative to the reference implementation.
Cache reuse crosses identity boundaries or serves features from stale frames.
Batching gains disappear below eight people while adding more than 20% latency at one or two people.

risk.description: Most encoder work may remain inherently per-person because inputs are pose trajectories, limiting gains to batching efficiency and window-cache reuse.

unavailable_inputs: Canonical method implementation
Representative crowded-scene track-length distributions
Pinned hardware and software environment
Profiler traces and deterministic numerical-equivalence tests
candidates.why_it_matters: A multi-person counter needs evidence that shared components actually reduce duplicated computation and that scaling claims do not hide identity-state memory or sacrifice per-person output fidelity.

candidates.name: Mass-Conserving Per-Person Count Ledger
build_steps: Decode each identity's reconstructed response into continuous count increments before any rounding.
Record increments in an identity ledger indexed by frame interval and track lineage, so overlapping windows cannot contribute the same response mass twice.
On high-confidence fragment re-entry, transfer the dormant ledger to the restored identity; on ambiguous association, hold increments in an unassigned escrow entry until resolution.
Apply rounding only once when an identity is finalized, and expose unresolved or unmatched ledger entries rather than folding them into another person.
Return the vector of finalized per-person counts with confidence and provenance; derive the scene total from that vector and verify conservation against the ledger.
candidates.hypothesis: A response-mass ledger with one final decode per identity will reduce boundary double counting, fragmentation duplication, and hidden reassignment errors while guaranteeing an auditable per-person output.

minimum_leakage_free_pilot.data: Use the frozen source-disjoint dev split with supplied tracks plus label-independent synthetic fragmentation, overlap duplication, and late re-entry.
minimum_leakage_free_pilot.protocol: Compare window-count summation, overlap-add followed by per-track decode, and overlap-add plus the lineage ledger; training remains unchanged and uses no per-person count or period labels.
measurements: difference between scene diagnostic and sum of emitted person counts

success: Conservation error between derived scene total and the sum of emitted per-person counts is exactly zero after finalization.
Boundary or fragment duplication contributes less than 1% of total decoded response mass.
AvgMAE under synthetic fragmentation improves by at least 10% relative to per-window count summation without degrading clean supplied-track AvgMAE by more than 2%.
failure: The ledger uses GT identity to transfer count mass at inference.
More than 5% of response mass remains unresolved at the declared finalization horizon.
The ledger improves only scene-total error while identity-matched per-person error is unchanged or worse.

risk.description: Incorrect lineage decisions can make bookkeeping confidently wrong; escrow and unresolved-output reporting must remain visible rather than forcing assignments.

unavailable_inputs: A canonical frame-level response representation
A frozen identity finalization and re-entry horizon
Track-lineage metadata in saved predictions
Official unmatched-person handling in the evaluator
closest_priors: Density-response integration in TransRAC and related RAC methods
Tracklet lineage graphs in multi-object tracking
candidates.why_it_matters: The scientific target is a vector of per-person counts, so the system needs an explicit invariant preventing overlap, fragments, and late identity decisions from creating or deleting count mass.
